derivations.title: Exact-count certificate simulation
derivations.claim: P^#P[1] ⊆ UP^CeqP, hence PH ∪ PP ∪ parityP ⊆ UP^CeqP
steps: Fix a total language accepted by deterministic polynomial-time computation using one value of a #P function f. Incorporate its deterministic query map into F(x)=f(q(x)); composition with a polynomial-time map preserves #P. The deterministic post-query acceptance test is a polynomial-time Boolean function b(x,j). A no-query computation can be represented by a dummy count.

Choose an explicit polynomial w(n) with 0≤F(x)<2^w(n). Use exactly w(n) nondeterministic bits, so every j in [0,2^w(n)) is guessed once, including zero. This strict upper bound avoids the endpoint bug from trying to encode 2^w with w bits.

Define A as well-formed pairs (x,j), with j exactly w(|x|) bits, satisfying F(x)=value(j). This is a total CeqP language: on valid pairs use GapP difference F(x)−value(j), and on invalid encodings use the constant nonzero gap 1.

Guess j, query A, and accept iff the answer is yes and b(x,j)=1. Only the unique correct j can survive, so the machine is unambiguous relative to this actual oracle on every input. It need not be unambiguous relative to arbitrary other oracles; STT Definition 5.2 explicitly uses the actual oracle.
PH⊆P^#P[1] is the strong Toda theorem used in STT Theorem 5.1. PP and parityP belong to P^#P[1] directly by comparing, or taking parity of, a single accepting-path count.

Under CeqP⊆parityP, replace the oracle in this same machine. UP^parityP⊆parityP^parityP=parityP follows from unconditional relativizing unambiguous-to-parity simulation and parity self-lowness. No relativization of the hypothesis occurs.

Under CeqP⊆AWPP, apply UP^AWPP⊆AWPP. Under CeqP⊆WPP, use UP^WPP⊆coCeqP and WPP=CeqP=coCeqP, where the final equality follows from WPP complement closure. These yield PH, PP and parityP in the indicated target.
derivations.not_claimed: The source theorem states the PH endpoint; the PP/parityP extension is the explicit construction above.

derivations.title: CeqP inside QMA suffices for the Vyalyi PH collapse
steps: For L∈PH use D1 to obtain F∈#P, polynomial count width w(n), and a deterministic acceptance predicate b(x,j). Define the total CeqP exact-count language A from D1.

Choose an injective polynomial-time pair encoding whose length ℓ(n) depends only on n and w(n), and satisfies ℓ(n)≥w(n). For example, encode x by prefixing its length in unary with a delimiter, then x and the fixed-width j. All guesses for a fixed x have exactly the same encoded length. Invalid encodings are no-instances of A.

The premise gives A∈QMA. Vyalyi Theorem 1 (also Marriott–Watrous Remark 3.5) gives A∈A0PP. Vyalyi Lemma 3 supplies a GapP function h0 and a polynomial p such that on a query z of length m, yes implies h0(z)>2^p(m), while no implies 0≤h0(z)<2^(p(m)−1). The nonnegative condition applies to every no-query string.

Set k(m)=m+2, h(z)=h0(z)^k(m), and S(m)=2^(p(m)k(m)). Polynomial products preserve GapP. Yes queries satisfy h>S(m), and no queries satisfy 0≤h<2^−k(m)S(m). All thresholds for guesses on x equal S(ℓ(|x|)).

Let H(x)=sum over all w(|x|)-bit j of b(x,j)·h(encode(x,j)). The predicate b and encoding are polynomial-time; GapP is closed under this exponentially many terms sum and polynomial-time selection. Therefore H∈GapP.

If x∈L, its unique correct count has b=1 and contributes more than S; every other contribution is nonnegative, so H>S. If x∉L, the correct count has b=0. Every included term is a wrong count, hence H<2^w ·2^−(ℓ+2)S≤S/4. The explicit FP function S(ℓ(n)) has polynomially many bits.
Thus H(x)−S(ℓ(|x|)) is a GapP function positive exactly on L, proving L∈PP. The proof never requires PP⊆A0PP, QMA complement closure, or the hypothetical inclusion relative to an oracle.

Exactly the same construction applies when L∈parityP, since one #P value determines its answer by a parity test. Thus the consequence also includes parityP⊆PP; no additional theorem or oracle assumption is required.
derivations.not_claimed: Vyalyi Corollary 1 states the stronger premise QMA=PP. This weaker-premise implication is an explicit adaptation of the proof, not a direct quotation of that corollary.

semantics_review.details: Finite transition lists preserve branch multiplicities. Halted accepting leaves count once, and all surviving branches must halt at the polynomial horizon. Arbitrary polynomial-bounded time-bound functions do not introduce advice because a single finite machine halts and its final count is stable.

Global bounds on accepting counts give total UP/FewP. GapP is a difference of actual #P functions. SPP is exactly 0/1, CeqP tests zero, PP tests positive, parityP tests odd. Switching signed GapP to #P for parity uses subtraction=addition mod2. Strict-negative PP conventions can be met by 2g−1.

Quantifies over every explicit natural-coefficient error polynomial and uses a power-of-two polynomial normalizer. Numerators are nonnegative and globally bounded by that denominator, exactly matching FFKL Definition6.1. Larger natural-coefficient polynomials dominate conventional polynomial error requests.

The normalizer is computed by a total concrete FP transducer; LWPP sees only unary input length. Signed nonzero normalizers agree with FFK Definition5.13; positive-normalizer conventions follow by multiplying gap and normalizer by f, giving f²>0. Complement uses f−g. No arbitrary input advice is hidden in FP.

A concrete polynomial-time transducer generates injectively encoded circuits from unary length. H,T,X,CNOT have explicit standard amplitudes and CNOT controls differ from targets. All input/witness/ancilla registers are disjoint. QMA quantifies over normalized pure witnesses and imposes soundness on every such witness; mixed states give convex combinations and no advantage. QCMA-to-QMA uses dephasing by copying the witness into fresh ancillas, compatible with the unitary-only circuit model.

Every binary input is yes or no, so oracle/subroutine substitutions apply on all queries. coQMA/coUP are defined complements, not self-complement claims.
